subject: Future Tech
title: The Lawson Criterion
description: Learn The Lawson Criterion in one minute.

hook.text: John Lawson figured out the fusion recipe in 1955: you need enough heat, density, and time—all at once.

buildup.text: The Lawson criterion says plasma must be hot enough, dense enough, and confined long enough to sustain net energy.

discovery.text: Triple product = temperature × density × confinement time. Cross the threshold and the reaction sustains itself.

twist.text: For 60 years, reactors improved one variable at a time but couldn't hit all three together. It's a three-body juggle.

climax.text: Modern superconducting magnets and better plasma control are finally pushing all three variables past the threshold.

punchline.text: Hot enough, dense enough, long enough. That's the recipe.

quiz.question: What three factors does the Lawson criterion require?
